laws.rule: Queensland Parks and Wildlife Service areas: obtain a camping permit before camping and display the camping tag or permit details at the campsite for the stay. Check park alerts and the specific area conditions before travel.
laws.heading: Parks and outdoor access

laws.rule: Queensland Parks and Wildlife Service says campfires are prohibited during fire bans and are not permitted at many parks and forests. Where fires are allowed, use provided fireplaces, obey local restrictions and do not collect firewood in the park.
laws.heading: Parks and outdoor access

laws.rule: Queensland says domestic pets are not allowed in national parks, with exceptions such as qualifying assistance animals. Dogs may pass through in a vehicle on public gazetted roads only if kept inside; do not stop at visitor sites. Some other conservation parks, forests and recreation areas allow dogs in specified places.
laws.heading: Parks and outdoor access

laws.rule: Queensland Parks and Wildlife Service prohibits drones in all camping areas of protected areas, recreation areas and forests, and in additional signed areas. Check the specific park rules and national CASA requirements.
laws.heading: Parks and outdoor access

laws.rule: Queensland specifies that campers must attend the campsite within 24 hours after the permit commences and must not leave it unattended for over 24 hours after arrival without a reasonable excuse.
laws.heading: Parks and outdoor access

culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: Queensland Parks asks visitors to respect First Nations culture. Rock art and other sites in parks and forests represent thousands of years of living culture and are easily damaged and irreplaceable: look at them and enjoy them, but do not touch or damage them. Stay on walking tracks.
culture-and-protocol.sacred_or_restricted_places: The caring-for-parks page does not list a statewide closed-site register. Follow park-specific notices for any restricted cultural areas.
culture-and-protocol.cultural_authority: Queensland Parks and Forests, Department of the Environment, Tourism, Science and Innovation.
culture-and-protocol.note: From the statewide 'Caring for parks and forests' visitor page, last updated 12 June 2026. Other park rules on that page (wildlife, fire, rubbish, pets) are not restated here.
